Let \(R_m=\mathbb Z/2^m\mathbb Z\), and let \(N_m\) be the desired number.

Modulo \(2\), the only square-zero \(2\times2\) matrices over \(\mathbb F_2\) are
\[
0,\quad E_{12},\quad E_{21},\quad 
\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
For two such matrices \(A,B\), the conditions \(A^2=B^2=AB=BA=0\) allow exactly these \(10\) residue pairs: \((0,0)\), and for each of the \(3\) nonzero nilpotents \(N\),
\[
(0,N),\quad (N,0),\quad (N,N).
\]

Now count lifts to \(R_m\).

If both \(A,B\) are even, write \(A=2A'\), \(B=2B'\). Then all four product conditions modulo \(2^m\) are equivalent to the same conditions for \(A',B'\) modulo \(2^{m-2}\). Each entry of \(A',B'\) has \(2\) lifts from modulo \(2^{m-2}\) to modulo \(2^{m-1}\), so the even-even contribution is
\[
2^8 N_{m-2}.
\]

Next consider a residue class like \((0,E_{12})\). A lift
\[
B=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\ c&d\end{pmatrix}\equiv E_{12}\pmod2
\]
has \(b\) a unit and \(a,c,d\) even. The equation \(B^2=0\) gives
\[
a+d=0,\qquad a^2+bc=0,
\]
so \(a\) can be any even element, \(b\) any unit congruent to \(1\pmod2\), and then \(c=-a^2/b\) is forced. Hence there are
\[
2^{m-1}\cdot 2^{m-1}=2^{2m-2}
\]
such \(B\).

For any such primitive \(B\), it is conjugate over \(R_m\) to \(E_{12}\). The matrices \(A\) with
\[
A\equiv0\pmod2,\qquad AB=BA=0
\]
therefore correspond to even matrices annihilating \(E_{12}\) on both sides, namely
\[
A=tE_{12},\qquad t\equiv0\pmod2.
\]
There are \(2^{m-1}\) choices for \(t\), and \(A^2=0\) automatically. Thus each nonzero residue class contributes
\[
2^{2m-2}\cdot 2^{m-1}=2^{3m-3}.
\]
There are \(9\) such nonzero residue-pair classes, so
\[
N_m=2^8N_{m-2}+9\cdot 2^{3m-3}.
\]

With \(N_0=1\) and \(N_1=10\), solving this recurrence gives

\[
\boxed{
N_m=
\begin{cases}
(11\cdot 2^m-3)\,2^{3m-3}, & m\ \text{even},\\[4pt]
(13\cdot 2^{m-1}-3)\,2^{3m-3}, & m\ \text{odd}.
\end{cases}}
\]

So this is the number of ordered pairs \((A,B)\).
